title: Personalized Hemodynamic Resuscitation Targeting Capillary Refill Time in Early Septic Shock: The ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2 Randomized Clinical Trial
shortTitle: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2: personalized resuscitation improved a hierarchical composite
summary: In 1,467 analyzed patients with early septic shock, a personalized protocol targeting capillary refill normalization improved a hierarchical composite of death, duration of vital support, and hospital stay versus usual care. The difference was driven mainly by shorter vital support, rather than demonstrated mortality reduction.
whyItMatters: Serial capillary refill can support a structured resuscitation assessment alongside fluid responsiveness and bedside echocardiography. The intervention was a treatment algorithm, not an isolated capillary-refill target.
limitations: Unblinded care and a hierarchical composite complicate attribution of benefit. Patients were managed in 86 ICUs, limiting direct extrapolation to all ED sepsis presentations.
population: Adults within four hours of septic shock in 86 centers across 19 countries.
intervention: Personalized hemodynamic protocol using capillary refill, pulse/diastolic pressure, fluid responsiveness and echocardiography.
primaryEndpoint: Hierarchical day-28 composite: mortality, duration of vital support, then hospital stay.
findings: 1,501 randomized; 1,467 included in the primary analysis.
evidenceNotes: Publisher abstract and selected indexed methods/conclusion passages reviewed; complete full text was not reviewed. Legal PMC12573117 manuscript identified. Publisher first-online date October 29 precedes December 9 print date.
